html:
A narrow gauge railway was built around St Kitts between 1912 and 1926 to carry cane from the estates to the central sugar factory at Basseterre. It circles most of the island.

Sugar had been the island's business since the 1640s, first on estates worked by enslaved Africans and after emancipation by poorly paid labourers. The central factory and the railway were an effort to keep the trade alive against beet sugar.

The government closed the sugar industry in 2005. Part of the line now runs as a scenic train for cruise passengers, through the fields and past the old estate houses, mills and the Brimstone Hill fort.
